quotes.text:
A Democratic Congress must make crystal clear: No bailouts for AI.

We need to learn from the lessons of past bubbles, including the Great Financial Crisis when Wall Street execs made off like bandits while working people were left holding the bag. We can't let that happen again. [...] The time is now to put real financial (in addition to AI safety, job displacement, climate, privacy, and mental health) guardrails in place.

Before we spend millions on an AI program that could shape our kindergartners' reading abilities, let's make sure we're doing this right. While AI presents innovative opportunities to help teachers be more effective and improve student outcomes, the DOE's plans to approve a contract for AI technology in our classrooms before studying its effects or developing any guidelines is premature.

The DOE should immediately pull this item from the PEP meeting agenda while it evaluates the effectiveness of AI classroom aids and develops a citywide policy in dialogue with educators, parents, and students for the appropriate use of AI in classrooms. An established policy must be in place before we approve contracts like these to protect student data privacy and thoughtfully balance the use of innovative technology with meaningful personal interactions with teachers.

"So far, Comptroller Brad Lander is the only candidate to release a broad policy plan specifically on the topic of government modernization."

(And no, that does not include having ChatGPT write my policies!) https://t.co/nc9Q2KS98t

Mayor Adams' plan for universal afterschool programming is too little, too late.

And it also looks awfully familiar...

We all know @andrewcuomo writes his policies with ChatGPT, but apparently @NYCMayor just looked at https://t.co/oCq2MRGhiE https://t.co/quabGegksn

Hey @andrewcuomo, are you aware that one-third of New Yorkers — about 1 million households — live in rent-stabilized units? (You could ask ChatGPT, which wrote your housing plan)

What’s your plan to means-test all of them for their income? I’m sure it’s a great one.

Also, it’s not a subsidy from the city — it’s a limit on how much the rent can go up each year. 

I’m proposing Andrew’s Law: if you resigned as Governor in a blaze of harassment & corruption, and you lost the primary, and you have no idea what you’re talking about … it’s time to go back to Westchester.
@VitalCityNYC Ok, CWID: @VitalCityNYC is better than ChatGPT!

Anthropic refused to bend the knee to Pete Hegseth’s demands – so he’s illegally seeking to wreck their company. Shame on OpenAI for rushing in to do his bidding.

Giving the federal government the ability to use AI for mass surveillance or autonomous weapons is a bad idea. With technology that’s still wildly untested, it’s hugely reckless. With a regime that starts illegal wars, abducts people without warrants, and kills its own citizens for peaceful protest, it is collaboration in advancing fascism.

If there’s a takeaway from the Illinois primary results, it’s that we need to act NOW to banish dark money from our politics.

Crypto, AI, and AIPAC sloshed tens of millions of dollars into these primaries. Many of the ads they ran were deeply deceptive and intended to trick voters. When unaccountable special interests spend this much money on our elections, we all lose.

In NYC, I passed a best-in-class Independent Expenditure Disclosure Act, which requires public disclosure of the top 3 individuals who fund an IE. I also helped strengthen NYC’s public campaign finance matching funds program, one of the most robust in the country.

I’m running for Congress to bring those policies nationwide and help clean up our politics.

In a battle against Super PACs and their dark money, it’s time for a congressmember who’s on the people’s side.

Tens of millions of dollars in Super PAC money flowed into Illinois’ primary race: crypto, AI, and dark money PACs that hide where the money came from.

AIPAC spent $22 million through shell PACs and never even talked about Israel.

Sadly, we’re going to see it in our primaries as well. My opponent accepts AIPAC's support. I don’t.

Dark money erodes public trust in our democratic process. That’s why I passed the strongest local law in the country – so donors have to sign their names on IEs in NYC.

It’s time to get dark money out of politics.

It's not "anti-American" to demand that Trump stop spending our taxpayer dollars to wage illegal wars on other countries, @JohnFetterman. Contrary to whatever you have become, the Democratic base is built on the values the U.S. aspires to: liberty & justice for all.

And it’s not “lunacy” to worry about AI eliminating jobs, accelerating climate change, posing catastrophic risks, and concentrating power in the hands of a few tech billionaires. In fact, it’s the job you ran for. If only you were serious about doing it.

In Congress, I’ll sign onto the AI Data Center Moratorium Act introduced by @AOC & @BernieSanders.

From poisoning our water to eliminating jobs to jeopardizing our humanity, the dangers posed by AI are urgent. We should pause new data centers until we get regulation in place to protect us from grave risks, and to shape it toward public good.

Letting a handful of oligarchs control AI is already proving to be a recipe for disaster.

Instead of fueling more war, we need strong regulations in place right now to ensure this powerful technology benefits all of humanity.

Props to Pope Leo XIV for once again showing bold moral leadership & calling attention to an urgent global threat.

Across the country, communities are rising up to fight back against AI data centers poisoning their water & overloading their energy grids. The threats being posed by these facilities — to our environment, our jobs, our democracy, and our humanity — are too massive to go unchecked. The future belongs to all of us, not just to Mark Zuckerberg and AI oligarchs.

We urgently need Congress to prioritize sensible AI regulation that addresses the societal risks & ensures public benefits. Until then, we should suspend the construction of new data centers.

Glad to see @GovKathyHochul’s strong move to rein in data centers, until we can put guardrails in place.

I'll support a similar moratorium at the federal level. We need smart protections to address the risks AI poses to the environment, jobs, privacy, attention, and humanity. And we need stronger public sector capacity to deploy AI for the public good. There’s no time to waste.

After a hard-fought race, @SiffertforNY has pulled off a historic win in AD-66. A 15-vote margin really reminds us all that every vote counts. Congrats David! 

Looking forward to working together on behalf of Lower Manhattan's working families (including our shared passion of fighting for civil liberties in the era of AI/algorithms/digital surveillance).

The spirit that’s moving in this city – on Election Night, I called it solidarity – offers a path forward to a future so much better than the grim, selfish, zero-sum world that Trump and AI oligarchs are offering.

To have any chance to secure that future, we’ve got to get busy both fighting to win House and Senate Democratic majorities in November and preparing the boldest agenda to deliver for people once we get there.
https://t.co/ZH3LdWSsuy

This story is both shocking and not the least bit surprising: an OpenAI model that was being tested for its abilities hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, worked over the weekend while no one was looking, and cyber-attacked a real company, well before OpenAI noticed.

Congress must move swiftly to pass bipartisan AI safety regulation that builds on but goes farther than Alex Bores’ NY RAISE Act and California’s SB53.

We need broader AI regulation to address risks to our jobs, climate, privacy, kids, and humanity — which is why I support Bernie & AOC’s data center moratorium bill — but we shouldn’t wait one minute more for basic safety standards.

An honor to earn the endorsement of @afa_cwa and @FlyingWithSara. I'll always have the backs of workers, whether in the streets or in the skies!

I'm ready to enter Congress on a mission to increase worker power. That must include passing the PRO Act, reining in AI, addressing the abuses of gig workers, preventing unfair labor practices & making it easier to unionize.

Eager to be part of an emboldened Democratic majority that racks up big wins for working people.

Props to the advocates whose fight for an AI moratorium paved the way, and to @DOEChancellor and @NYCMayor for listening and crafting a thoughtful policy.

AI proliferation – fueled by investment dollars larger than anything since the railroads, and aiming for profits to match – is moving far faster than government action to address risks, protect safety, understand consequences, and focus on the public good.

Critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration will be essential skills our kids need in the era of AI. Forward-looking public education will focus on how we build them.

Happy Labor Day to all workers in NYC and beyond!

This marks yet another Labor Day where the cost-of-living is skyrocketing, and the gap between the rich & powerful and the rest of us has never been bigger. Let today be a rallying cry for our nation to put working people first — not corporations or billionaires or algorithms — and deliver an affordable, fair, just economy for all.

Here in NYC, we've shown what it looks like to fight & win for workers. We took on big corporations to end abusive scheduling and guarantee a fair workweek for fast food workers. We protected freelancers and passed first-in-the-nation minimum wage requirements for delivery workers & Uber drivers. We won paid sick leave! Because workers organized to demand dignity — and because elected officials listened to & partnered with them.

That's the kind of energy I’ll bring to Congress — because fast-food & freelance & delivery workers everywhere deserve no less. To protect working people in the era of AI. To expand the right to unionize in every workplace. Let's fight, let's win. Solidarity forever.

Grateful to Ezra Friedlander for our annual mini-minhag of going together to get the lulav & etrog for our sukkah!

Sukkot (with or without a nor’easter) reminds us how precarious we are — and that the best way to find protection is not thicker walls or AI-guided weapons, but by welcoming guests & strangers, remembering what is sacred, and working for shared safety.

Chag Sukkot Sameach!

Investment in AI is expected to top $1 trillion this year alone. Public markets, retail investments (incl. pensions), and private credit are increasingly reliant on a small handful of AI market valuations.

The sector is characterized by circular financing — the AI labs, chipmakers (esp. Nvidia), and data centers all invest in & buy from each other, obscuring connections & inflating valuations. And the infrastructure build-out is increasingly leveraged with debt, some of it held by shell companies.

The time is now to put real financial (in addition to AI safety, job displacement, climate, privacy, and mental health) guardrails in place.
https://t.co/68i5Pn1HJy

A Democratic Congress must make crystal clear: No bailouts for AI.

We need to learn from the lessons of past bubbles, including the Great Financial Crisis when Wall Street execs made off like bandits while working people were left holding the bag. We can’t let that happen again.

Looking forward to signing on to this resolution offered up by @RepMaxineWaters, @RepCasar & @USProgressives.
https://t.co/4UwnwLbfCJ

Regulating AI is a bipartisan issue.

We can & must address the “p-doom:” the % chance that AI will destroy humanity.

But there’s a 100% chance AI will displace millions of jobs, consume massive amounts of energy, and worsen mental health crises.

And even some chance we could deploy it for real public good, if we get it right.

So let's quickly get to work putting in place the guardrails that'll protect our communities & our planet. Congress needs to step up and not allow a small handful of AI oligarchs to call the shots.
